title: Just sort it! A note on the LP behind rank-one anti-loop edits
why_wsp: Replaces the sparse LP that computes v in the AHA rank-one anti-loop edit W' = W + u v^T of Qwen3.5-0.8B down_proj matrices with a closed-form sort over neuron activation statistics, no solver and no LLM editor.
domain: LLM math reasoning (removing thinking loops; MATH-500, GSM8K)
editor: none (closed-form sort; replaces LP solver of AHA [Khamis et al.] / Barry LP)
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B, down_proj of layers 15 and 19 (MLP width 3584)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: rank-one edit using 8 neurons per layer: 'we take the 8 neurons whose activation has the smallest coefficient of variation' (Abstract); two layers

headline_results.claim: Sort edit 67.0% vs LP edit 67.4% vs unedited 9.5% on 1000 problems (seed 0)
headline_results.quote: the sorted edit scores 67.0% on 1000 problems (MATH-500 and GSM8K) against 67.4% for the LP edit and 9.5% for the unedited model
the paired difference is -0.4 points, with 95% confidence interval [-2.9, +2.1], inside a non-inferiority margin of 5 points declared before the runs.

headline_results.claim: Three further seeds; LP-free dose arm also within margin
headline_results.quote: On three further sampling seeds the difference is -0.6 points, interval [-2.0, +0.8], and -0.8 points, interval [-2.3, +0.6], when the dose is set without the LP.

headline_results.claim: Shared neurons carry most of LP push
headline_results.quote: the neurons shared by the two supports carry 95% (layer 15) and 88% (layer 19) of the mean push

headline_results.claim: LP edit does not separate looping vs productive tokens
headline_results.quote: the LP edit pushes the looping tokens by -0.79 and the productive ones by -0.70 at layer 15

headline_results.claim: Knapsack control (8 largest-mean neurons) also within margin: 66.2%, diff -1.2 [-3.7, +1.3] (Table 1 row)
headline_results.quote: The knapsack-like rule knap_k8 is also within the margin

cost.quote: the search of a layer, essentially the two solves, takes 3 to 11 seconds, about 2.2 minutes over the 20 layers, on one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
a dense constraint matrix with about 43 million nonzeros.
The whole work took one day, 16 November 2026.

baselines_and_controls: LP edit (AHA), unedited base, knap_k8 (largest-mean neurons) control, sortd_k8 (dose from delta, no LP). Constant steering along u not tested ('a steering arm is the natural next control').
runs_and_variance: Seed 0 plus three further sampling seeds (1,2,3); paired 95% CIs; 'the seeds measure the sampling noise on fixed edits; they do not replicate the pipeline that produces u' (Sec 3). Pre-registered protocols.
verification: statistical: pre-registered non-inferiority test with paired CIs
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no LLM editor); finding is that edit acts as 'a nearly constant bias along u'
limitations_stated: 'we tested one model and one run of the pipeline that produces u'; constant-shift steering control not run; post hoc sortd_k8 split by benchmark (worse on MATH-500).
cites_or_builds_on: AHA: Khamis, Tutunov, Bou Ammar 'Who needs an LLM to program an LLM?' blog
N. Barry 'Can a linear program do weight-space programming?' blog
notes_for_survey: Shows the LP in the solver-based anti-loop edit can be replaced by sorting neurons by coefficient of variation with no measurable accuracy loss on Qwen3.5-0.8B; argues the informative part is the direction u. Paper states the work was done by Claude (Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5) under author supervision in one day.
